clue.text: Entanglement that makes yours truly shut up

parts.note: the setter referring to themself, giving me
sh is the command to be quiet

explanation.surface: A tangle that leaves the speaker silenced.
explanation.definitionFit: A mesh is a net or tangle of threads, so being caught in one is an entanglement.

clue.text: A trick? Be first to give a signal

indicators.note: the word be is told to come first, ahead of the article and the trick

parts.note: taken as written
a con is a swindle or trick

explanation.surface: Someone advised to get in first with a ruse in order to send a message.
explanation.definitionFit: A beacon is a fire or light used as a warning signal.

clue.text: Musical character parted, finishing prematurely

indicators.note: the word stops before its proper end, so its last letter is lost

parts.note: cleft means split or parted

explanation.surface: A musical figure leaves the stage before the show is over.
explanation.definitionFit: A clef is a symbol, a character written on the stave to fix the pitch of the notes.

clue.text: Shelter wide open with its roof off

indicators.note: in a down clue the roof is the top letter, so the first letter goes

parts.note: yawning means gaping wide open

explanation.surface: A ruined shelter gapes open to the sky, its roof gone.
explanation.definitionFit: An awning is a canvas canopy giving shelter from sun or rain.

clue.text: Sort of traveller in the distance, wise man coming around

indicators.note: the wise man's word wraps round the distance word

parts.note: a seer is a prophet or sage
afar means far away

explanation.surface: A distant traveller and a sage arrive together.
explanation.definitionFit: A seafarer is a sailor, one kind of traveller who goes by sea.

clue.text: Examination of various cells in a hospital?

definitions.text: Examination of various cells in a hospital?

parts.words: Examination of various cells in a hospital?
parts.note: cells suggest prison or monastery rooms, but these are red and white cells tallied in a test on a patient's sample

explanation.surface: Someone inspecting the rooms of a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: This medical test counts the numbers of the different cells in a sample of a patient's blood.

clue.text: The sort of setback that doesn't affect Mum or Dad

definitions.text: The sort of setback that doesn't affect Mum or Dad

parts.words: The sort of setback that doesn't affect Mum or Dad
parts.note: Mum and Dad read the same backwards, so turning them round leaves them unchanged

explanation.surface: A family misfortune that somehow leaves the parents untouched.
explanation.definitionFit: A setback is a reversal of fortune, and words like these survive being read backwards.

clue.text: Article stuffed into broken slate that may fill a gap?

indicators.note: the article is packed inside the jumbled word
a broken slate has its letters shattered and rearranged

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A grammatical article is pushed into a smashed roof slate to plug a hole.
explanation.definitionFit: A sealant is a substance applied to fill and seal gaps and joints.

clue.text: Periodical lacking power, we're told

indicators.note: the phrase says we hear the word rather than see it

parts.note: weakly means feebly, without strength

explanation.surface: A magazine without much influence, so people say.
explanation.definitionFit: A weekly is a newspaper or magazine published every week, a type of periodical.

clue.text: Short fellow taking companion to a dance

indicators.note: the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: chap is an informal word for a man
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A small man brings a friend along to a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The cha-cha is a Latin American ballroom dance.

clue.text: Policy U-turn makes you go mad, then collapse

parts.note: to flip is to lose one's temper or sanity
to flop is to fall down heavily or fail

explanation.surface: A government reversal drives you crazy and then falls apart.
explanation.definitionFit: A flip-flop is a sudden reversal of a stated policy or position.

clue.text: A short campaign organised with many special effects?

indicators.note: the words are arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A brief, well-run campaign full of flashy effects.
explanation.definitionFit: Phantasmagoric describes a shifting, dreamlike succession of images, as produced by spectacular special effects.

clue.text: Encouraging a number to join in judicial inquiry

indicators.note: the number goes inside the inquiry word

parts.note: a hearing is a trial or inquiry before a court
ten is a number

explanation.surface: It is uplifting when several people take part in a court case.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartening news gives courage and cheer, so it is encouraging.

clue.text: Fur coats that could sound right for a seductive woman

indicators.note: the word heard aloud fits the seductive woman

parts.note: a minx is a flirtatious, impudent young woman

explanation.surface: Furs that would suit a femme fatale.
explanation.definitionFit: Minks are coats made from the fur of the mink, a small animal.

clue.text: Head of state falling short

indicators.note: the word falls short of its end, losing its last letter

parts.note: Maine is a US state

explanation.surface: A head of state who doesn't measure up.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, head means chief or principal, as in the main road.

clue.text: See denouncer of Tories be consumed by an envy out of control

indicators.note: the word be is swallowed inside the other letters
the letters run wild into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An envious rage swallows a critic of the Conservatives.
explanation.walkthrough: Aneurin (Nye) Bevan, the Labour minister who founded the NHS, called the Tories 'lower than vermin'. 'See' simply invites you to look.
explanation.definitionFit: This Welsh Labour politician famously denounced the Conservatives as lower than vermin.

clue.text: Document one reproduces — what's needed?

indicators.note: the question invites the solver to find the required item inside the preceding words themselves

explanation.surface: A question about what is required to copy a document.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition and the wordplay: the letters run across 'documenT ONE Reproduces', and the clue asks what a copier needs to reproduce a document.
explanation.definitionFit: A photocopier needs this powdered ink to reproduce a document, so it is exactly what is needed.

clue.text: Sports official about to get released with game finally covered

parts.note: re means concerning or about

indicators.note: the released word covers the letter taken from game

parts.note: free means set loose

indicators.note: the last letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A referee about to be freed once the match is wrapped up.
explanation.definitionFit: A referee is the official who enforces the rules in sports such as football.

clue.text: Hiding rubbish around university

indicators.note: the rubbish word goes round the letter

parts.note: rot means nonsense

explanation.surface: Concealing junk near a college campus.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiding is a heavy defeat, and a rout is a crushing defeat.

clue.text: What was demanded of Hardy maybe, an act presaging doom

definitions.text: What was demanded of Hardy maybe
definitions.meaning: the dying Nelson is said to have asked 'Kiss me, Hardy' of his flag captain at Trafalgar
an action that seals someone's ruin

explanation.walkthrough: Hardy was Nelson's captain at the Battle of Trafalgar (1805), and the dying admiral's request is a famous British anecdote.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means an action that ensures failure, and Nelson's dying request was literally a kiss.

clue.text: This writer's old as visualised

parts.note: the setter saying 'I am', shortened to I'm
aged means old

explanation.definitionFit: To image something is to picture it in the mind, so imaged means visualised.

clue.text: Liveliness of goblin with energy coming to the fore

indicators.note: the letter moves to the front of the word

parts.note: a sprite is an elf or goblin
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A goblin's vitality as it surges forward.

clue.text: Done fantastically by fellow, finished finally when asked for

indicators.note: the letters are reshaped wildly

parts.note: man means a fellow or chap

indicators.note: the last letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Something made brilliantly by a man and finished at last, just as requested.
explanation.definitionFit: Something available on demand is supplied whenever asked for.

clue.text: Daughter skating apparently — one to fall by chance?

explanation.surface: A girl on skates who might easily take a tumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Dice are thrown and fall at random, deciding games of chance; dice is often used as a singular.

clue.text: A drip's getting worse, becoming lots of quick-flowing water

indicators.note: the letters deteriorate into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, with the apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A leaking tap gets worse until it is a torrent.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapids are stretches of a river where the water flows fast over rocks.

clue.text: The attraction of a match in which no one loses

definitions.meaning: something that pulls in crowds, an attraction

definitions.text: a match in which no one loses
definitions.meaning: a game ending level is a tied result

explanation.definitionFit: Draw means both a crowd-pulling attraction and a tied game.

clue.text: Had a meal at back of pub, as is natural

indicators.note: the meal word goes behind the pub word

parts.note: an inn is a pub
ate means had food

explanation.surface: Someone eats at the back of a pub, as one naturally does.

clue.text: Guerrilla with remarkable claim relating to a type of warfare?

definitions.text: relating to a type of warfare?

parts.note: Che Guevara was the famous Argentine-born guerrilla leader

indicators.note: read as re-markable, the word can be marked out again in a new order
